messages:
tara: Quick thread about Go SDK generator ergonomics. Ran into confusing behavior around the constructor ctx and streaming lifetime in our onboarding sample.
aj: what happened?
tara: sample app does auth refresh w/ short timeout. We call NewGenerator(ctx, ...) and immediately Stream(). If handshake is slow and ctx cancels, constructor returns error but a reader goroutine stays alive. Hard to debug in CI.
devon: ack. Are we sure the reader is started before handshake completes? Could be a startup ordering race.
tara: yep. I instrumented: NewGenerator spawns readLoop before awaiting handshakeFuture. If handshake fails/cancels, we don't signal the loop to stop.
aj: we should be explicit in docs about what the ctx controls (handshake vs lifecycle). But more importantly fix the leak non-breaking: don't start readLoop until handshake success or bind a cancel channel.
devon: small patch idea: in constructor, after initiating handshake, do a select { case <-handshakeDone: spawnReader(); case <-ctx.Done(): return nil } so we never spawn reader on cancelled ctx.
tara: I implemented that locally and added a test that simulates a stalled handshake (fake server sleeps) and cancels ctx; test asserts no extra goroutines after constructor returns. Fix works.
aj: nice. Can you open a PR with unit + integration test and doc update? PR title: "go: guard generator read loop on handshake or ctx cancel". Add me + devon as reviewers.
devon: separate thought: API ergonomics. Some customers want NewGenerator to tie to lifecycle (ctx controls entire life), others want handshake-only ctx and control lifecycle separately. Changing signature is breaking. Options: 1) Add NewGeneratorWithLifecycle(ctxLifecycle) or 2) add Start/Close pair so constructor never spins up network work until Start(ctx) is called.
tara: Start/Close seems clean: constructor becomes cheap and safe in short-lived contexts. But it's a breaking behavior change for existing users who expect NewGenerator to be ready.
aj: propose phased approach: patch now to prevent leaks (non-breaking), update docs to recommend long-lived ctx for lifecycle or call Start explicitly in sample; then open an RFC proposing Start/Close or a two-ctx constructor for v0.15.
devon: agree. Also sweep internal onboarding/sample apps and fix any that pass short timeouts to NewGenerator. We should add a lint rule in our examples that warns about using context.WithTimeout in constructor calls.
tara: will do the sample sweep and update onboarding repo. I'll include a short recommended snippet in docs showing both patterns:
```
// recommended: long-lived generator bound to background lifecycle
ctx := context.Background()
g, _ := client.NewGenerator(ctx, modelID)
// use g.Stream/Next, close when done
// or explicit start API (future): g.Start(ctx)
```
and the anti-pattern:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 50*time.Millisecond)
g, err := client.NewGenerator(ctx, modelID) // avoid if you plan to call Stream immediately
```
aj: also add a unit test that runs on CI with a tiny handshake delay to catch regressions. Tag it flaky=false.
ciaran-bot: PR created (#6189) with patch + unit tests + docs change. CI queued (1 retry allowed for flaky jobs) :robot_face:
devon: after merge, let's update CHANGELOG and a short note in the migration guide explaining ctx semantics and recommended patterns.
tara: PR ready for review, linking to sample updates. thanks all. :thumbsup:
